themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 this week versus a baseline average of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 8.69)—suggesting a potential contamination event or distribution system failure affecting East Flatbush residents.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2300% spike)
Z-score of 8.69 indicates highly anomalous statistical deviation
Timeframe: acute spike emerging within last 7 days
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine if contamination event or main break occurred; check for boil water notice or advisories
Interview affected residents about water discoloration, taste, or odor; cross-reference with utility service requests

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped to 3 last week, up 500% from a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.0), suggesting either new illicit street vending activity or a targeted enforcement operation in East Flatbush.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints last week vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% increase)
Z-score of 5.0 indicates statistically significant outlier
Timeframe: spike appeared within last 7–14 days
reporting_angles: Request enforcement data from DOE/Business Integrity Commission to determine if targeted enforcement operation occurred last week
Canvass commercial corridors (Flatbush Ave, Church Ave) to observe vendor activity and interview vendors and residents about enforcement intensity

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 74 two weeks ago, up 265% from a baseline of 20.2 per week (z-score: 4.13), indicating a significant acute episode of construction, street activity, or events concentrated over a single period.
evidence: 74 street/sidewalk noise complaints two weeks ago vs. 20.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (265% spike)
Z-score of 4.13 confirms statistically significant deviation
Timeframe: concentrated spike from 2 weeks ago; recency suggests investigation window may be narrowing
reporting_angles: Cross-reference with DOB permits and event calendars from two weeks ago to identify construction projects, street fairs, or events that triggered spike
Interview residents in highest-complaint neighborhoods to pinpoint location and source of noise; determine if ongoing

themes_detail.label: Lead Exposure Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints increased to 6 two weeks ago, up 182% from a baseline of 2.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.96), raising concerns about elevated lead hazards in residential units or drinking water in East Flatbush.
evidence: 6 lead complaints two weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (182% increase)
Z-score of 4.96 indicates highly anomalous spike
Timeframe: spike concentrated within past 2 weeks; aligns with water quality concerns (potential overlap in causation)
reporting_angles: Investigate whether lead spike correlates with water quality spike (lead leaching from pipes); coordinate with DEP on water testing
Request HPD data on lead violations, remediation orders, and inspections in East Flatbush within last 30 days; interview tenants in affected buildings

themes_detail.label: Dumpster and Sanitation Issues
themes_detail.summary: Dumpster complaints reached 5 two weeks ago (700% above baseline of 0.6 per week, z-score: 6.29) and sanitation worker/vehicle complaints hit 4 last week (540% above baseline of 0.6, z-score: 3.94), indicating waste management or collection service disruption in the district.
evidence: 5 dumpster complaints two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 6.29)
4 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (540% spike, z-score: 3.94)
Timeframe: overlapping spikes within past 14 days suggest coordinated or cascading service disruption
reporting_angles: Request Sanitation Department records on collection schedules, route changes, labor shortages, or equipment breakdowns in East Flatbush within last 2 weeks
Photograph overflow dumpsters and blocked curbs; interview residents and business owners about service delays and street cleanliness
